instrument_name: California Labor Code 2810.5 (wage theft notice at hire), leginfo copy via Wayback 2026-08-31
authority: California Legislative Counsel (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov)
figure_or_rule_carried: 2810.5(a)(1): at hire the employer gives each employee a written notice "in the language the employer normally uses to communicate employment-related information to the employee" (pay rate(s) and basis, allowances, regular payday, employer name/DBA, main office address, telephone, workers compensation carrier, sick-leave statement, emergency/disaster declaration, other Labor Commissioner items). (a)(4): for H-2A workers an additional section in Spanish, given on the first day; the worker may also ask for English. (b) changes notified in writing within 7 calendar days unless shown on a timely wage statement. (c) excludes state/local employees, overtime-exempt employees and CBA employees paid 30 percent above minimum wage. Last amendment Stats. 2023 Ch. 451 (AB 636), eff. 2024-01-01. Fixes the language rule that US-FEDR3-009 reached only through the Labor Commissioner FAQ.

instrument_name: Indiana Code 22-2-2-8 Statement of hours and wages; furnishing employees; posting law (IC 2026, Title 22 Art. 2)
authority: Indiana General Assembly (iga.in.gov)
figure_or_rule_carried: (a) each pay period the employer furnishes each employee a statement with at least: (1) hours worked, (2) wages paid, (3) a listing of the deductions made. (b) a sworn statement of that information on commissioner demand; records open to inspection. (c) a one-page poster: current Indiana minimum wage, basic rights, contact information. No language clause and no retention period in the section. Source history printed: P.L.37-1985, P.L.144-1986, P.L.48-2009 SEC.1. Replaces the provisional FindLaw copy.

instrument_name: La. R.S. 38:2301 (Title 38 Part VI Payment of Prevailing Wages): repealed
authority: Louisiana State Legislature (legis.la.gov)
figure_or_rule_carried: Page text: "PART VI. PAYMENT OF PREVAILING WAGES. 2301. Repealed by Acts 1988, No. 18, 1; Acts 1988, No. 90, 1, eff. June 27, 1988." The state prevailing-wage section no longer exists, so no state prevailing-wage rule applies to Louisiana payroll (federal Davis-Bacon still applies on federal projects). This row records the repeal; the section itself is not in force.

instrument_name: Maine DOL Paid Family and Medical Leave: Frequently Asked Questions for Employers (July 2026)
authority: Maine Department of Labor, Paid Family and Medical Leave
figure_or_rule_carried: FAQ 4: for calendar years 2025-2027 the joint employer+employee contribution rate is 0.5 or 1 percent of wages by employer size; no more than 0.5 percent may come from the employee. Employers with 15 or more employees contribute 1 percent and may deduct up to half from wages; fewer than 15 employees contribute 0.5 percent and may deduct the whole amount. FAQ 5: wages as for Maine UI wages; premium excludes amounts above the annual base limit set by the U.S. Social Security Administration (figure not stated). FAQ 18: self-employed opt-in premium 0.5 percent of self-employment income for 2025-2027. FAQ 49-51: with an approved private plan the employee deduction is capped at 0.5 percent of wages until at least 2028. Consistent with the 1.0 percent ceiling of 26 MRSA 850-F in US-ME-P5-1-002. Tier note: the exact 2026 rate rests on an authority FAQ (A.3) plus the A.1 ceiling; no A.2 rate table was located.

instrument_name: Minn. Stat. 181.032 Required statement of earnings by employer; notice to employee
authority: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
figure_or_rule_carried: (a) earnings statement each pay period, written or electronic; electronic statements need employee access to an employer computer in working hours and availability for 3 years. (b) must show: employee name; pay rate(s) and basis; meal/lodging allowances; total hours (unless chapter 177 exempt); gross pay; list of deductions; amounts deducted and paid under 268B.14 (paid leave premium); net pay; pay-period end date; employer legal and operating name; main-office physical and mailing address; employer telephone. (c) paper on 24 hours notice, then ongoing. (d) written hire notice (rates, allowances, PTO accruals, exempt status, possible deductions, pay days, employer identity/address/phone). (e) notice given in English with commissioner text offering another language; if requested the employer provides it in that language; signed acknowledgment kept. (f) written changes before they take effect. Language rule for US-MQ-03.

instrument_name: Minn. Stat. 177.42 Definitions (prevailing wage on state-funded projects, sections 177.41 to 177.44)
authority: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
figure_or_rule_carried: Definitions for 177.41-177.44. "Project" = demolition, erection, construction, alteration, improvement, restoration, remodeling or repair of a public building, structure, facility, land or other public work financed in whole or part by state funds (also when acquisition, predesign, design or demolition is state-financed). "Prevailing hours of labor" cannot exceed 8 per day or 40 per week. "Prevailing wage rate" = hourly basic rate plus contributions for medical, pensions, injury compensation, unemployment, life/disability insurance, vacation and holiday pay, apprenticeship and other bona fide fringe benefits; cannot be less than a reasonable and living wage; includes truck-hire rental rates for 177.44. Establishes that a Minnesota state prevailing-wage regime exists (public projects only). Rates and thresholds are not in this section.

instrument_name: Unemployment Insurance Minnesota: Agent Self-Service System page
authority: Minnesota Department of Employment and Economic Development, UI Minnesota
figure_or_rule_carried: An agent must be registered as an agent with Minnesota UI through the Self-Service System and holds an 8-digit Minnesota UI Agent Identification Number. The employer/client then completes the online agent authorization/role assignment using that ID, choosing role(s) and access type (view only, or update and submit). The page describes an online authorization and no paper power-of-attorney form. Page date not shown in the saved file.

instrument_name: NHES employer handbook NHES 0041 (user-downloaded copy): May I Use An Authorized Agent?
authority: New Hampshire Employment Security
figure_or_rule_carried: An employer that wants to designate an authorized agent to receive NHES mailings or to represent it in claim or tax matters must make a request in writing to NHES; the request must be made by the employer and signed by a duly authorized employee whose position or title is stated. No form number is named in that passage. EDITION CAVEAT: the saved text carries no edition marker (the caller records R-8/16); inside, the UI taxable wage base is given as 14,000 "beginning with the first quarter 2012" and a rate table runs to 2017, so the handbook is 2016-17 vintage. Use it for the agent procedure only, never for a figure; confirm the procedure is still current with NHES.

instrument_name: NH RSA 275:48 Withholding of Wages (Wayback copy 2026-03-21)
authority: New Hampshire General Court (gc.nh.gov)
figure_or_rule_carried: I: no employer may withhold or divert wages unless (a) required or empowered by state or federal law, including payroll taxes; (b) the employee gave written authorization for a lawful deduction (listed items include health, welfare, pension and apprenticeship fund contributions, charities, housing and utilities, savings funds, uniforms, group insurance, any mutually agreed purpose without financial advantage to the employer); (d) on the employee written request, listed items (cafeteria plans, child care, loan instalments, recovery of accidental overpayment under conditions) provided the employer gives a written itemized accounting at least once a month. Re-read of the section carried by US-NH-P5-1-001; no prevailing-wage content.

instrument_name: City of Jersey City, Payroll Tax page (Ordinance 18-133)
authority: City of Jersey City (Tax Collector)
figure_or_rule_carried: Employer payroll tax created by Ordinance 18-133 (final approval by Municipal Council 2018-11-20): 1 percent of gross payroll of employers located in Jersey City. Exempt: employers with quarterly gross payroll under 2,500 USD; wages of Jersey City residents; US, NJ, county, municipal, school and interstate bodies and their agencies; foreign-state insurers (N.J.S.A. 17:32-15); charitable organizations. Payroll = remuneration subject to federal income tax withholding for services performed in Jersey City, or performed elsewhere but supervised from Jersey City (generally per Form 941). Returns and payments quarterly: Apr 30, Jul 31, Oct 31, Jan 31 (postmarks not accepted). Employer may NOT deduct or withhold the tax from employee pay (Ordinance 304-21; the page misprints "18-33" once). Card payments carry a 2.20 percent fee, e-checks 0.50 USD. The page cites no N.J.S.A. enabling statute; the N.J.S.A. 40:48C-14 / S.B. 4219 references in earlier notes are not confirmed by this page.

instrument_name: City of Newark, Payroll Tax page
authority: City of Newark, Division of Tax Abatement and Special Taxes
figure_or_rule_carried: Newark payroll tax equals 1 percent of wages for services performed within Newark, applied to services supervised from Newark or wages of employees who primarily report to a Newark location. Reduced rate 0.50 percent for employers whose workforce is MORE THAN 50 percent Newark residents, with residency documentation. Returns quarterly, due by the 30th day following the end of each quarter (April, July, October, January). The page names no ordinance or statute and does not say whether the tax may be withheld from wages. Discrepancies with earlier rows: US-NJR3-001 wrote "50 percent or more" (page: more than 50 percent) and "employer-paid, not withheld" (not stated on the page).

instrument_name: NJ Division of Taxation, Employer Withholding (Payroll) Taxes page (last updated 09/28/26)
authority: New Jersey Division of Taxation
figure_or_rule_carried: Page directs employers to the tables or methods in the New Jersey Gross Income Tax Instructions for Employers to compute withholding; the saved text names no online withholding calculator. Withhold NJ income tax from resident employees (unless taxed at a higher rate in another state) and from nonresidents working in NJ, with an Employee Certificate of Nonresidence exception; withhold 7 percent from payments to unregistered unincorporated contractors; year-end filings (NJ-W-3, W-2, W-2G, 1099, 1094/1095) must be electronic. Lists "Treasury Launches New Automated Payroll Service" as a recent topic (no detail in the file). No local payroll tax or POA content on the page.

instrument_name: NM DWS Power of Attorney/Authorization of Agent form (ES-905 Rev. 6/08)
authority: New Mexico Department of Workforce Solutions (Unemployment Compensation)
figure_or_rule_carried: UI agent authorization form: employer appoints an attorney-in-fact/agent to act in its name, receive confidential information and perform UI functions checked: All Unemployment Matters, All Claims Matters, All Tax Matters, Appeals; may change the official mailing address. Must be signed by a sole proprietor, partner or corporate officer, contain data verifiable with Division records, and be NOTARIZED. Supersedes any earlier authorization for the subjects checked; stays in effect until written cancellation or a later authorization; a third party holding a copy may act under it. Letterhead is "Workforce Transition Services / Division of Unemployment Compensation" (old agency naming): confirm with DWS that Rev. 6/08 is the form in use.

instrument_name: 11.1.2 NMAC Public Works Minimum Wage Act Policy Manual (DWS Labor Relations)
authority: New Mexico Department of Workforce Solutions, Labor Relations Division
figure_or_rule_carried: Rule issued by DWS under Section 13-4-11(C) NMSA 1978. 11.1.2.8(A): every state or political-subdivision contract or project over 60,000 USD for construction, alteration, demolition or repair of public buildings, public works or public roads that employs mechanics or laborers must state minimum wages and fringe benefits not below the prevailing rates the director determines for the project. Annual survey period runs July 1 to June 30; determinations stay valid until superseded. Establishes the New Mexico prevailing-wage regime and its threshold for payroll scoping. The Act text itself (13-4-10 to 13-4-17 NMSA) was NOT read; the published rate determinations are not in this file.

instrument_name: Utah Code 34-28-3 Regular paydays; statement of total deductions (version effective 5/13/2014; Wayback copy 2016-09-06 plus 2026-05-19 version index)
authority: Utah State Legislature (le.utah.gov)
figure_or_rule_carried: (1)(a) wages paid at regular intervals no longer than semimonthly; (1)(b) within 10 days after the pay period closes; (1)(d) yearly-salaried employees may be paid monthly on or before the 7th of the following month. (4) if a deduction is made, the employer furnishes on each regular payday a statement showing the total amount of each deduction. (5) employers licensed under Title 58 ch. 55 (construction trades) give a written or electronic pay statement on payday: name, base rate, pay-period dates, hours if hourly, amounts and reasons withheld (state and federal income tax, Social Security, Medicare, court-ordered), total paid. (6) deductions only if court order, law, written employee authorization, hearing-officer offset or qualifying 401(k)-type plan; (8) 30-day change window for plan elections. No language clause. Currency: the 2026-05-19 index lists only this version, marked Current Version; amendments after that date are not verified.

instrument_name: Utah State Tax Commission Form TC-737 Power of Attorney and Declaration of Agent (Rev. 9/26)
authority: Utah State Tax Commission
figure_or_rule_carried: Taxpayer appoints agent(s) as attorney(s)-in-fact to receive and inspect confidential tax information and act as the taxpayer could, unless limited; power excludes receiving funds, substituting agents and disclosing information to anyone other than the Commission. One taxpayer/account per form; if left blank, all tax matters; the taxpayer may list acts NOT authorized (sign returns, amend, reallocate payments, represent in Commission proceedings, etc.). The taxpayer signature must be notarized; a new form revokes prior powers unless the box is checked. Organization filers list every authorized person.

instrument_name: Utah DWS Unemployment Insurance Power of Attorney / Authorization of Agent Form (Rev. 08/24; Wayback 2026-05-19)
authority: Utah Department of Workforce Services, Unemployment Insurance
figure_or_rule_carried: UI agent authorization: employer (corporation, partnership or individual) appoints an agent as attorney-in-fact for "all matters affecting unemployment insurance taxes", with separate check boxes for unemployment tax matters and for claims matters (determinations, hearing notices, appeals, benefit charges; option to receive correspondence through SIDES; broker number field). Notary seal required; signed by an authorized officer; supersedes prior POA; valid until rescinded by letter or superseded. Fax (801) 526-9377.

instrument_name: Virginia Employment Commission: Employer Self-Service (ESS) page - ID.me login and third-party access
authority: Virginia Employment Commission
article_or_section: ESS page: Instructions for Tax Preparers / Third Party Administrators / CPAs
figure_or_rule_carried: From 2026-08-01 ESS is reachable only with an ID.me login (action required by 2026-07-31); employers under 25 employees may also use eForms. A TPA/CPA user profile may link up to 250 VEC tax accounts; the EMPLOYER must send the invitation using the same email address the TPA/CPA registered with ID.me. The page describes an invitation process and names no paper power-of-attorney form. iFile (Virginia Tax) no longer accepts the VEC account number from 2026-08-01 (use FEIN). Job aids on ID.me/TPA access are linked as PDFs (not downloaded).

instrument_name: Code of Vermont Rules 24-090-003 Minimum Wage, Section VI Wage Statements (Cornell LII mirror)
authority: Cornell Legal Information Institute (mirror of the Vermont Secretary of State rule)
article_or_section: Section VI; statutory authority 21 V.S.A. 383 et seq.; effective 2004-09-01, amended 2006-02-20 and 2009-01-01
figure_or_rule_carried: Section VI: each employer delivers to each covered employee with the pay, each week, a detailed written statement showing at a minimum gross pay and hours worked, hourly rate and all deductions fully itemized (including number of meals for which a deduction is made and gross meals deductions unless full room and board is charged). Service employees submit a signed weekly tip report; the employer keeps those reports 3 years. TIER B: the text is a university mirror, not the Secretary of State publication; it reads consistently with the Vermont DOL WH-13 passage in US-VT-P5-2-004 (A.3). The official SOS text remains not obtained.
